name: One mark
why: 10: the one cut is made on the whole rail of length 10.

name: Two marks
why: 18: either cut first costs 10, and the second cut is on a piece of 8.

name: The order matters
why: 16: cut at 3 first (7), then 1 on the piece 0–3 (3), then 5 on 3–7 (4), then 4 on 3–5 (2).

name: Marks out of order
why: 22. Sort the marks first: the stretches are between neighbouring marks.

name: Middle first is not best
why: 26. Always cutting the mark nearest the middle of the piece gives 27.

name: Marks near the ends
why: 199: whichever goes first costs 100, the second 99.

name: Twelve marks
why: Trying every order of 12 cuts is 479,001,600 orders: far too slow. The table of stretches has 14 × 13 / 2 cells.

name: Twenty marks
why: Recursion without a memo solves the same stretches again and again: about 3²⁰ calls here.

name: 150 marks
show: 150 random marks on a rail of length 10⁹
why: About 150³/6, half a million split checks: under a second. Memoised recursion is also fine: it is at most 150 calls deep.

name: 150 evenly spaced marks
why: Many splits tie here; any of them gives the same total.
